description:
SnipSnaps helps you clean up your Mac in quick, focused review sessions — both your photo library and the files piling up in your folders.

PHOTOS
Swipe through recent photos, screenshots, videos, screen recordings, large photos, Live Photos, bursts, photos from this day in past years, random shots, or similar-looking groups. Keep the shots that matter, mark the ones you do not need, and delete them when you are ready.

FILES (Mac)
Pick a folder — Downloads, Desktop, Documents, or any folder you choose — and review what is taking up space. SnipSnaps surfaces everything, large files, old files you have not touched in months, screenshots, and duplicates. Anything you remove moves to the Trash, so it is always recoverable.

Use SnipSnaps to:

- Review your newest photos before clutter builds up
- Clear old screenshots and screen recordings
- Find similar-looking groups and keep the best shot
- Clean out Downloads and other folders by size, age, or type
- Move unwanted files to the Trash with a swipe or a keyboard shortcut
- See how many photos and files, and how much storage, you have cleared

SnipSnaps works entirely on your Mac. It asks for Photos access only so you can review and delete the photos you choose, and it only ever touches the folders you explicitly grant. Files you remove go to the Trash — nothing is deleted permanently without your confirmation, and nothing ever leaves your device.
promotionalText: Clean up your photo library and clear out cluttered folders — review by size, age, or type and send the junk to the Trash.

reviewNotes:
SnipSnaps requires no account, no sign-in, and no network access — all processing happens locally on the Mac.

There are two review surfaces:

1) PHOTOS — Grant Photos access when prompted. The app reads the local photo library to present review sessions. Deleting selected photos goes through the system Photos API, which shows a macOS confirmation dialog and moves the assets to Recently Deleted.

2) FILES (macOS) — The app has NO file-system access until the reviewer explicitly grants a folder. Click the + (Add Folder) button and choose a folder such as Downloads or Desktop in the system open panel. SnipSnaps then lists files in that folder by category (Everything, Large, Old, Screenshots, Duplicates). Removing a file moves it to the Trash (fully recoverable) via a security-scoped bookmark limited to the granted folder — files are never deleted permanently and no other locations are accessed.

TO EXERCISE DELETION DURING REVIEW:
- Photos: ensure the review account's photo library has a few images.
- Files: click + and add the Downloads or Desktop folder (or make a temporary folder with a few sample files), then swipe or use the keyboard shortcuts to review. Removed items appear in the Trash and can be restored.

KEYBOARD: Left arrow = keep, Right arrow = remove, Delete = remove, Space = Quick Look, Cmd-Z = undo, Esc = exit review.

App Sandbox is enabled; entitlements are limited to user-selected file access, app-scoped bookmarks, and Photos-library access.

privacy.photoLibraryPurpose: Accesses the user's photo library on device to display review sessions and delete only the photos the user explicitly selects.
privacy.fileAccessPurpose: Accesses only folders the user explicitly grants via the system open panel, persisted as app-scoped security-scoped bookmarks, to review and move selected files to the Trash. No file contents leave the device.
